dedupe_keys.name: keep calm and bank on household survey on panic driven bank runs after the svb collapse bis working paper 1119

description: This study asks whether news of a large bank failure raises the risk of runs on other banks, and whether public communication can contain it, using the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank on 9 March 2023 after an exceptionally rapid run. A household survey fielded afterwards recorded perceptions of bank and deposit risk, portfolio preferences, willingness to switch bank and knowledge of the events, and embedded information experiments that isolate the causal effect of news and official statements on intentions to withdraw deposits. It was written by Olivier Coibion, Yuriy Gorodnichenko, Francesco Grigoli and Damiano Sandri and published as BIS Working Paper 1119 on 4 September 2023. Coverage is US households. The 61-page paper is free as a PDF; the page read gives no reuse terms or data access. Findings: SVB news raised withdrawal intentions, mainly into other banks and cash, while Federal Reserve communication and information on deposit insurance reassured depositors and political statements swayed mainly their own voters. Caveats: it measures stated intentions in a survey, not actual withdrawals. For simulation it provides behavioural parameters for depositor panic and the damping effect of official communication in agent-based and contagion models of bank runs. It is related to the Two Centuries of Systemic Bank Runs database record in this catalogue.
